clue.text: To escape, go by plane

definitions.meaning: to flee or run away, as a frightened bird or fugitive does
to travel by air, literally getting airborne

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for fleeing and also a literal description of boarding an aircraft and flying.

clue.text: Homeless woman happy to settle in alcove

indicators.note: one word comes to rest inside the other, so the synonym for happy is placed within the alcove word

parts.note: a bay is a recess or alcove in a wall
glad means happy

explanation.surface: A cheerful homeless woman finds a nook to settle into.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial term for a destitute woman who carries her possessions around in carrier bags.

clue.text: Studies concerning publicity

parts.note: re means concerning or about
ads, short for advertisements, are publicity

explanation.surface: Someone is researching matters to do with advertising and promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: To read a subject is British usage for studying it at university, as in reading law.

clue.text: After very little time, beg for some work

indicators.note: the time abbreviation comes first in the answer, with the begging word placed after it

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time, a tiny sliver of it
to ask is to beg or request

explanation.surface: After a moment someone pleads to be given a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A task is a piece of work to be done, a job or assignment.

clue.text: This person cuts variety of lilac, a flowering shrub

indicators.note: the word for the speaker slices into the middle of the rearranged letters
a variety is a different form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the setter speaking of themselves is me

explanation.surface: A gardener prunes a lilac, a flowering shrub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This person' is the setter, and 'cuts' means the setter's word slices into the rearranged letters, not that anything is pruned.
explanation.definitionFit: The camellia is an evergreen shrub with showy rose-like blooms, related to the tea plant.

clue.text: One eventually finds a kind of bullet

definitions.meaning: someone who tracks things down and so locates them in the end
a round that leaves a visible trail of light so its path can be seen

explanation.surface: A searcher finally discovers a particular type of ammunition.
explanation.definitionFit: One who traces things eventually finds them; separately it names luminous ammunition.

clue.text: Shout "ouch", being cowardly

parts.note: to yell is to shout
ow is an exclamation of pain like ouch

explanation.surface: Someone cries out in pain and is branded a coward for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is an informal word for lacking courage, as in a yellow streak.

clue.text: My teacher, first to express words of encouragement

parts.note: my and well are both exclamations of surprise
a don is a university teacher

indicators.note: first to points at the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A pupil's tutor is the first to offer praise.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is what one says to praise or congratulate someone on an achievement.

clue.text: Letters man read aloud

indicators.note: the clue says the word is spoken, so a word with the same sound is entered

parts.note: a man is male

explanation.surface: A man reads out some correspondence.
explanation.definitionFit: Post is the collective term for letters and parcels delivered.

clue.text: Machine produces articles for use on both sides of the Channel

parts.note: la is a French definite article, from the far side of the Channel

parts.words: for use on both sides of the Channel
parts.note: the matching English definite article completes the pair, one article from each side of the English Channel

explanation.surface: A tool is made with parts usable in both Britain and France.
explanation.walkthrough: The Channel is the English Channel between England and France, so one article is French and one English.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathe is a machine tool that spins a workpiece against a cutter.

clue.text: Cake for future Guide?

definitions.meaning: a chocolate cake, dense and baked in squares
a junior member of the Girl Guides who will move up to Guides later

explanation.surface: A cake intended for a girl who will join the Guides?
explanation.walkthrough: Brownies are the junior branch of the Girl Guides (the British equivalent of Girl Scouts).
explanation.definitionFit: A chocolate traybake and a young girl in the junior section of guiding share this name.

clue.text: Scientist's dull routine: woman's cross!

definitions.note: read as scientist is, the apostrophe-s linking definition to wordplay

parts.note: a rut is a boring, fixed routine
her means belonging to a woman
to ford is to cross a river

explanation.surface: A scientist complains about tedium while a woman is angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scientist's' is read as 'Scientist is'; 'cross' is a verb, not the adjective for angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest Rutherford was the New Zealand-born physicist who split the atom.

clue.text: Distinguished area in US city

parts.note: august means distinguished or venerable

explanation.surface: A distinguished district within an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Augusta is the state capital of Maine and a city in Georgia famous for golf.

clue.text: Test now in the afternoon?

definitions.meaning: once past noon the morning is a former thing: ex (former) plus am (morning)

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is cryptic: in the afternoon it is no longer a.m., so it is ex-a.m.
explanation.definitionFit: An examination is a test, and the short form is the everyday word.

clue.text: Amateur needed by play manager

indicators.note: needed by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A theatre manager has to rely on a non-professional.
explanation.definitionFit: A layperson is a non-professional, someone without expert training in a field.

clue.text: Forest kept by German horticulturist

indicators.note: the forest is held inside the abbreviation for German

parts.note: Arden is the forest of Shakespeare's As You Like It, in Warwickshire

explanation.surface: A German looks after a forest as a horticulturist.
explanation.walkthrough: The Forest of Arden is an English woodland area made famous by Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who tends plants for a living or as a hobby is a horticulturist.

clue.text: Track advertisement for future programme

definitions.meaning: a path or the marks left by someone passing
a short preview promoting a forthcoming broadcast

explanation.surface: A TV channel promotes a track for an upcoming show.
explanation.definitionFit: A trail is a path, and also British usage for a trailer, a promo for a coming show.

clue.text: Writer so upset and angry when taken into care

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the two letters are rearranged
the anger word is placed inside the care word

parts.note: wild means very angry

explanation.surface: A writer is distressed and furious at being taken into care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'care' is used as written; 'when' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish playwright and wit of The Importance of Being Earnest.

clue.text: Wash bottle out and dry with these, after soaking

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Rinse out a bottle and dry it, after leaving it to soak.
explanation.definitionFit: Large absorbent cloths used to dry oneself after a soak in the tub.

clue.text: Lout is exhausted

explanation.definitionFit: As one word it is an idle loafer; as two words, dead beat, it means worn out.

clue.text: Pupil left to join person getting income

parts.note: an earner is someone who earns money

explanation.surface: A pupil leaves to join someone who earns a wage.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil is one who is studying, a student or trainee.

clue.text: Not fit, having polished off bun with ale

indicators.note: polished off suggests the food and drink are demolished and so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone feels unwell after scoffing a bun and a pint of ale.
explanation.definitionFit: Unable means lacking the capacity or competence to do something.

clue.text: Person working on roof loses head subsequently

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, which is dropped here

parts.note: a slater lays slates on roofs

explanation.surface: A roofer's decapitation comes afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses head' drops the S from SLATER.
explanation.definitionFit: Later means afterwards, at a subsequent time.

clue.text: Do very little to get bread

definitions.meaning: a shaped mass of baked bread

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to lounge around idly; the noun is a baked mass of bread.
